events.title: ISM Services PMI (September)
events.why_it_matters: First activity print after Friday's +29k NFP miss; services are most of US GDP and will test whether labor slowing is demand-wide or just hiring freeze.
events.what_to_watch: Consensus ~55.0–55.7 after August 55.4; employment and prices-paid vs S&P flash 58.7.

events.title: US–Iran war: Iran says Hormuz stays closed until US meets 7 conditions
events.why_it_matters: Seven-month war plus a contested Strait of Hormuz keeps a regime-level oil, shipping, and inflation premium in US and global risk assets.
events.what_to_watch: Any mediator talks vs Camp David 'war council' follow-through; tanker attacks; Trump 'one way or another' timeline.

events.title: Brent holds ~$100–102 as Hormuz logistics, not just barrels, bite
events.why_it_matters: Crude transits have partially recovered via escorts/bypasses, but tanker rates, insurance, and refined-product tightness keep a consumer-tax and CPI input in place.
events.what_to_watch: Brent holding above $100; diesel/jet cracks; any reopening signal vs new shipping attacks.

events.title: China Golden Week (National Day) travel vs spend
events.why_it_matters: Holiday volume is the live read on whether PBoC/mortgage support is thawing households, or whether property-scarred consumers still travel more and spend less.
events.what_to_watch: Official trips/revenue after Oct 7; per-capita spend vs 2025's ~911 yuan; outbound vs domestic mix.

events.title: California record heat wave / wildfire-smoke risk
events.why_it_matters: Late-season extreme heat lifts power demand and fire risk into SEMICON West week, a local but tradeable utilities/insurance overlay.
events.what_to_watch: CAISO peaks, outage/fire news, Bay Area air quality into Oct 13–15.

events.title: September NFP miss: +29k, U3 4.2%, wages +3.0% y/y
events.why_it_matters: Payrolls badly missed ~+90k consensus, prior months revised −60k, and wage growth slowed — collapsing October hike odds while leaving a growth-scare tail.
events.what_to_watch: Whether ISM employment, claims, and Oct 14 CPI confirm cooling without a demand collapse.

events.title: Eurozone September flash HICP 3.8% y/y (energy spike)
events.why_it_matters: Hottest headline since 2023, energy 18.8% y/y, tests the ECB's post-September 25 bp hike 'hold' into the Oct 29 meeting.
events.what_to_watch: Final HICP Oct 16; core staying ~2.5%; Lagarde tone vs energy pass-through.

events.title: OPEC+ holds November output targets unchanged
events.why_it_matters: Core producers paused after finishing the 1.65 mb/d unwind; actual barrels remain far below quotas because of the Iran war, so the signal is 'no extra supply'.
events.what_to_watch: Next monthly review Nov 1; compliance vs war-disrupted output.

events.title: Camp David Iran 'war council' after Hormuz rejection
events.why_it_matters: Senior US principals met as Iran restated Hormuz stays shut; raises odds of a military or sanctions step before US midterms rather than a 7-day reopen deal.
events.what_to_watch: Carrier movements, new sanctions, any public Trump timeline.

events.title: US–China Busan truce extended to Jan 10, 2027
events.why_it_matters: Two-month extension past Nov 10 removes the near-term tariff cliff through holiday shipping, without resolving chips, EVs, or the 2027 expiry.
events.what_to_watch: Formal USTR exclusion notices; Board of Trade follow-through; APEC (Nov) prep.

events.title: US–China $60bn '30-for-30' tariff-relief lists
events.why_it_matters: Recommended MFN-style cuts on ~$30bn each way (US consumer goods vs China ag/energy/medical) would ease goods inflation and farm exports if implemented.
events.what_to_watch: Domestic legal process and start dates; soybeans still excluded; chips/EVs/batteries out.

events.title: China factory PMI back above 50; PBoC PSL cut + mortgage subsidy
events.why_it_matters: Official manufacturing PMI 50.1 plus a 25 bp PSL cut, bigger relending quotas, and a 1 ppt first-home subsidy (from Oct 1) is the latest counter-cyclical push amid property drag.
events.what_to_watch: Golden Week spend; whether property and private-survey PMIs follow official 50.1.

events.title: Korea September exports record $120.9bn, chips +263% y/y
events.why_it_matters: Semiconductor exports $60.3bn validate the AI-memory boom already signaled by Micron and keep Korea/Taiwan tech as a global growth engine even with $100 oil.
events.what_to_watch: ASML Oct 14 and SEMICON West commentary on HBM/DRAM tightness vs China demand.

events.title: Micron FQ4 beat and ~$61.5bn FQ1 revenue guide
events.why_it_matters: Memory pricing/AI capex confirmation is the strongest corporate offset to oil-and-tariff stagflation fears in the tape.
events.what_to_watch: Peer commentary at SEMICON West; whether guide holds if China/AI capex slips.

events.title: Tokyo September core CPI +2.7% y/y (hot lead for national CPI)
events.why_it_matters: Well above ~2.3% consensus after BoJ's Sept hike to 1.25%, keeping another hike in play at the Oct 29–30 meeting (just outside this window).
events.what_to_watch: National CPI Oct 23; yen and JGB reaction if energy keeps core sticky.

events.title: CIT probes July 2026 global Section 301 forced-labor tariffs
events.why_it_matters: Near-universal 10–12.5% 301 duties on ~60 economies are the administration's replacement for struck IEEPA tariffs; a vacatur would be a multi-sector regime shift.
events.what_to_watch: Supplemental briefs due Oct 16; any stay/vacatur language in the coming weeks.

events.title: US August goods-and-services trade balance
events.why_it_matters: Deficit print is a read on tariff-front-running vs oil import bill after the truce extension.
events.what_to_watch: Goods deficit vs oil; China-related import volumes.

events.title: FOMC minutes of Sept 15–16 25 bp hike to 3.75–4.00%
events.why_it_matters: Markets have already crushed October hike odds to ~17–25% after Williams' 'no urgency' and the NFP miss; minutes show how close 50 bp was and the bar for Oct 27–28.
events.what_to_watch: Dissent, labor vs oil-inflation split, any 'one more hike late 2026' language.

events.title: Graham Act: USTR/Presidential notification on Russia/Iran secondary tariffs
events.why_it_matters: PL 119-111 requires up to 500% tariffs on Russian goods and up to 100% secondary tariffs on top buyers of Russian energy / evasion facilitators — a live China/India/Turkey shock.
events.what_to_watch: Covered-country list and rates in the ≥10-day congressional justification before Oct 18 imposition.

events.title: PepsiCo Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: First major staples print of Q3; tests whether $100 oil, tariffs, and weak volumes are breaking pricing power.
events.what_to_watch: Organic volume vs price; FY guidance; commentary on input costs.

events.title: University of Michigan consumer sentiment (prelim, October)
events.why_it_matters: Household inflation expectations and buying conditions are the transmission from $100 oil into demand destruction and Fed reaction; September final was a weak 48.1.
events.what_to_watch: 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations vs sentiment level.

events.title: Delta Air Lines Q3 2026 earnings (jet-fuel stress test)
events.why_it_matters: Bellwether airline vs Brent >$100; Q3 plan assumed jet fuel ~$3.15/gal after a record $3.93 in Q2.
events.what_to_watch: Unit fuel, premium demand, Q4 margin guide, capacity cuts.

events.title: Q3 bank kickoff — JPM, WFC, C, GS (Oct 13) and BAC (Oct 14)
events.why_it_matters: Sets the tone for NII under a hiking Fed, credit quality after labor cooling, and capital-markets activity.
events.what_to_watch: NII guides, charge-offs/reserving, trading/IB, commentary on consumer delinquency.

events.title: UnitedHealth Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Managed-care and Dow bellwether; medical-cost trend and 2027 guidance move the whole healthcare complex.
events.what_to_watch: MCR, membership, any FY/2027 reset.

events.title: September existing-home sales (NAR)
events.why_it_matters: Housing is the rate-sensitive sector most exposed to the 2026 hiking cycle; August was a weak 3.98m SAAR with pending sales down 4.1% y/y.
events.what_to_watch: SAAR vs ~4.0m, inventory, mortgage-rate commentary.

events.title: SEMICON West 2026 (San Francisco)
events.why_it_matters: Flagship chip-equipment gathering as the industry talks $1tn revenue and AI capacity; guidance tone can move semis into ASML week.
events.what_to_watch: HBM/advanced-packaging capacity, China tool demand, NVIDIA/keynote color.

events.title: China September trade data (GACC)
events.why_it_matters: Exports have been China's growth engine; the print shows whether tariff-truce front-running is still inflating shipments before the Jan 10, 2027 expiry.
events.what_to_watch: Export y/y vs August +18.6%; IC/high-tech vs US/ASEAN mix. Preliminary due Oct 14.

events.title: September CPI — energy-driven headline, cooler core expected
events.why_it_matters: Last major inflation print before the Oct 27–28 FOMC; consensus ~+0.5–0.6% m/m headline (~3.7% y/y) vs core ~+0.2% m/m / 2.4% y/y.
events.what_to_watch: Gasoline vs shelter/supercore; a hot core would reprice the collapsed October hike odds.

events.title: ASML Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Global WFE/EUV bellwether; confirms or fades the AI-capex boom after Micron and Korea exports.
events.what_to_watch: 2026/27 bookings, China vs TSMC/HBM mix, gross margin.

events.title: September PPI and advance retail sales
events.why_it_matters: PPI (~+0.5% m/m expected) is the pipeline into CPI/PCE; retail sales test whether $100 oil is already destroying goods demand after the NFP miss.
events.what_to_watch: Core PPI vs control-group retail; gasoline-ex sales.

events.title: Eurozone September HICP final
events.why_it_matters: Confirms or revises the 3.8% flash that already challenged the ECB's measured hold.
events.what_to_watch: Revisions to energy/services; any core uptick from 2.5%.

events.title: CIT supplemental briefs due in Section 301 global-tariff case
events.why_it_matters: Judges ordered answers on statutory basis, standing, and vacatur scope — the next hard date before a written decision.
events.what_to_watch: Government's §2411 theory; whether plaintiffs seek nationwide vacatur vs as-applied relief.

events.title: Graham Act primary/secondary tariff imposition deadline
events.why_it_matters: Statutory 30-day clock from the Sept 18 signing; even a waiver/narrow list would be a market event, a China/India hit would not.
events.what_to_watch: Federal Register rates, covered countries, any presidential waiver.

events.title: Taiwan gray-zone pressure vs silicon-shield (no invasion priced as imminent)
events.why_it_matters: US sources still see full invasion unlikely near-term, but coast-guard quarantine tactics are the slow-burn risk to TSMC power/shipping — a chip-supply tail, not the base case.
events.what_to_watch: ADIZ/coast-guard counts; any arms-sale delay after the Trump–Xi summit.

top_risks: Iran/Hormuz: no ceasefire, strait stays closed on Tehran's 7 conditions, refined-product tightness keeps Brent ~$100+ and headline CPI hot.
Graham Act Oct 8 notification / Oct 18 imposition: up to 100% secondary tariffs on top buyers of Russian energy (China/India/Turkey) stacked on existing 301 duties.
Oct 14 CPI: energy-led 3.7% headline with a non-cooperative core would reverse the collapse in October FOMC hike odds.
CIT Section 301 case: a vacatur or a loss both reprice the entire post-IEEPA global tariff architecture.
Growth scare: +29k NFP plus oil-taxed consumers — if ISM/retail/UMich confirm, risk-off in cyclicals even as the Fed pauses.
top_opportunities: Fed pause reprice: October hike odds already ~17–25%; a cool core CPI plus dovish minutes would extend the post-NFP duration rally.
AI/memory complex: Korea exports, Micron guide, ASML (Oct 14) and SEMICON West (Oct 13–15) can keep tech as the growth offset.
US–China truce to Jan 10, 2027 plus $60bn 30-for-30 lists: near-term tariff cliff is cut if lists are implemented.
Energy mean-reversion if any credible Hormuz reopen/escort breakthrough — the largest single risk-on switch in the tape.
Bank/UNH week (Oct 13–14): if NII/credit and medical-cost trend hold, financials/healthcare can lead a 'higher-for-longer but not hiking now' tape.
summary: The tape is still a two-factor regime: a live US–Iran war with Hormuz restricted and Brent near $101, versus a labor-market miss (+29k) that crushed October FOMC hike odds to ~20%. Policy is two-sided — a US–China truce to Jan 10 and $60bn relief lists cut the near-term China tariff cliff, while the Graham Act's Oct 8/18 secondary-tariff clock and the CIT challenge to global Section 301 duties keep trade risk binary. Q3 earnings open with PepsiCo then banks/UNH/ASML against an AI-memory boom Korea and Micron have already validated.
